_doc: The Mission Builder (R. Talsorian, Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode, SPM p.28 procedure, p.102 Mission Builder/Tracker sheet), as data for MissionBuilder (src/meta/mission_builder.gd). Every board offer goes through its steps in the sheet's order: who's hiring (clients), what's the mission (mission_types), the focus (focus), payment (payment), the twist (a hook only for now: gig.twist = null). Labels and framing lines are our own short paraphrases, never the book's text; the dice and row positions are the book's. Rows marked HOUSE-RULE are our readings of how a row plays here.

zones._why: HOUSE-RULE: which People of Night City / Mission Items category a place belongs to (SPM p.50, p.73 name the four zones but leave the choice to the player). Outskirts: a place in an outskirts district or a badlands scene. Otherwise the place's Security Code (its own, else its district's, NC2045 p.7): street_max and below Street/Combat Zone, corporate_min and above Corporate/Upscale; in between the district's profile decides (street_profiles Street, corporate_profiles Corporate), else Moderate/Community.

fallback._why: HOUSE-RULE: when a zone's Mission Items have nothing the objective can play (no data in the Outskirts, no person in Moderate), the next category in this order is used.

clients._doc: Who's hiring: People of Night City, SPM p.50-51. The book rolls the category on 1d10 (1-3 Corporate, 4-6 Moderate, 7-9 Street, 10 Outskirts); here the place's zone sets it (zones). Corporate, Moderate and Outskirts roll 1d10, Street 2d10 (2-20). Labels are our paraphrase of each row's type of person.

mission_types._doc: What's the mission: Mission Types, SPM p.72, 1d100 in 50 rows of two. objective: the gig objective it plays as (data/gen/objectives.json; the gig kind follows, Campaign.OBJECTIVES), or null while the game has no module for it: `needs` names the module (or 'social' / 'vehicles' for rows that need a non-combat or driving system). A roll on a disabled row is rolled again. framing: our one-line pitch for the board ({target} the target faction, {item} / {the_item} / {item_short} the focus). HOUSE-RULE: which existing objective an enabled row plays as is our reading; each is noted in `why` where it isn't obvious.

rows.why: chaos played as a firefight that ends when nobody is left

focus._doc: The focus: Mission Items/MacGuffins, SPM p.73. The book rolls the category on 1d6 (1-2 Corporate/High Tech, 3 Moderate/Community, 4-5 Street/Combat Zone, 6 Nomad/Outskirts); here the place's zone sets it (zones), then the category's die picks an item among those the objective can play (a roll on one it can't is rolled again). `as`: how an item plays. data: the file a data theft pulls; object: the package a snatch carries; captive: the person a rescue walks out; mark: the person an assassination puts down; wreck: what a sabotage or a gang hit ruins; vehicle, site: nothing yet (no vehicle play, no follow-up gigs). label/short/marker are ours: the board and brief, the marker over it on the map, the debrief line.

debrief._why: Our lines for the debrief, by objective: won, then not.
data: The {item_short} is out of the NET and with the client.
assassinate: {The_item} won't be a problem any more.
sabotage: {The_item} is ruined along with the machine.
eliminate: Nobody is left to hold on to {the_item}.
escort: {The_item} made the rendezvous in one piece.

rows.label: a journalist's notes on local fixers
a memory chip of hot data
word of the next Night Market
directions to a pre-war supply cache

payment._doc: Payment, SPM p.28 step 4: set from the core book's job pay (CPR core p.381: Easy 500eb, Typical 1,000eb, Dangerous 2,000eb per person; gigs.json `pay` is that rate for the two-person starting crew, flat per gig) and sometimes paid in information, a favour or goods instead of eb. HOUSE-RULE rates (the book gives none): 1d10 per offer, rows below; a non-eb payment keeps eb_share of the eb and adds the thing. information: an intel token (Campaign.intel): while the crew holds it, every offer on the board shows whether it will run into a complication (the Closed Question Oracle asked ahead, Complication.likelihood), and taking one spends it. favour: a token kept in the campaign (Campaign.favours): one free Med Bay Treatment of a Critical Injury, or one free Night Market item costing up to market_cap_share of the job's rate. goods: one item into safehouse storage worth at most goods_share of the job's rate (and at least a third of that), drawn from what the Night Market and the fixer sell today. Unique offers pay eb (their blurb promises double pay).

twist._doc: The twist, SPM p.28 step 5 (Plot Twists, SPM p.75-76): not built yet. Every gig carries twist: null; MissionBuilder.twist is the step a twist module fills.
